To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a fully automated approach that uses a wearable backpack to collect thermal imagery of building interiors, and generate a 3D point-cloud representation of the building’s interior that includes the thermal properties of the building elements, such as walls, floors, ceilings, furniture, and plug loads, and that the 3D representation can be visualized interactively and annotated to identify and document “hot spots” and thermal and moisture leaks.

we propose a novel approach to construct a thermal 3D point-cloud of the building interior, and that we demonstrate that the proposed approach can be used for thermal characterization of building interiors.

we developed a fully automatic approach based on wearable sensors for the generation of a “thermal 2.5D point cloud” of building interiors, and we demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach by collecting data from a building, visualizing and annotating the thermal and visible 2.5 D point clouds, and comparing the results to those obtained by manual inspection.
